Does longer foam rolling work better?
Not necessarily, a new RCT (J. Hofer et al., Aug 2026):
57 men randomized to 2 min, 10 min, or no hamstring foam rolling. Flexibility improved similarly in all groups, no Group×Time interaction, so foam rolling didn’t beat passive rest, and 10 min wasn’t better than 2 min. No changes in stiffness, strength, or creatine kinase either. Bottom line: no dose-response effect, and doubts foam rolling beats rest.
